current.text: Westbrook, Schroder and DeRozan have left the Kings. LaVine and Huerter remain.
Experts expect his usage to rise now that the other playmakers are gone. His assists could return to about 6 and his minutes to about 33.
He is a projected starter with Acuff, LaVine, Hunter and Murray. Coach Ham calls him the Kings' best player.
Mike Miller runs the Kings offense this season. It is not clear whether the offense will run through Sabonis.
Experts do not expect Maxime Raynaud to cut his minutes or the Kings to bench him for Raynaud.
The Kings may trade him. Toronto has talked to them about him before, and Sacramento might try to dump his contract.
Experts disagree on what a trade would do to his value. One says he would keep most of it. Another says a good team could use him as a 23-minute backup because he cannot defend or shoot.
His FG% should recover from last season's 54%, and he should miss fewer games.
The Kings are projected near the bottom of the West, with a Vegas win total of about 22.
The Kings want to stay out of the relegation zone, so experts expect him to play whenever he is healthy.
In category leagues he is worth a round 3 to 4 pick, not a first-rounder. About 25 USD is a fair auction price. His best case is about 13th and his worst case about 55th.

durable.text: He is a strong FG% anchor on high volume and an elite rebounder.
He commits many turnovers, which hurts the TO category clearly.
He is an unselfish passer who posts big assist and rebound numbers when the offense runs through him. Many of his assists come from dribble handoffs, so he needs the ball to rack them up.
He has never been a steals or blocks player and is a very poor shot blocker.
He is not a good three-point shooter.
He is a much better points league player than category league player. His game is hard to build around when he is taken early in category leagues.
In 2025-26 he pulled his hamstring before the season, then had a rib injury and then knee problems.

note: Experts put him at 24 to 25 USD and round 3 to 4 in category leagues. That matches his Yahoo value of 26 USD and is far below the 41 USD our league paid last season and his 39.3 USD ESPN average cost, so do not pay points-league prices. He fits a punt TO build that wants FG% and rebounds, with assists as a bonus. Early in the season, check whether Mike Miller's offense runs through him (assists near 6, about 33 minutes), whether his FG% gets back near 58%, and any trade news.
